Files are text, one record per line, pipe separated: `key|group|amount|tag`. They can be many gigabytes: the jobs run in small containers, so a function must not keep the whole file (or a list of all its lines) in memory.

## `scan.largest_orders(path)`

The five largest orders of the export.

Returns the five largest amounts as `(amount, line number)` pairs (line numbers start at 1), largest first; on equal amounts the earlier line comes first. Fewer pairs if the file has fewer lines.

"""exportkit: reports over large text files."""


def largest_orders(path):
    """The five largest orders of the export."""
    with open(path) as fh:
        rows = [line.rstrip("\n").split("|") for line in fh.read().splitlines()]
    numbered = [(int(row[2]), number) for number, row in enumerate(rows, 1)]
    numbered.sort(key=lambda pair: (-pair[0], pair[1]))
    return numbered[:5]

def longest_same_host(path):
    """The longest streak of the same account in the export."""
    with open(path) as fh:
        keys = [line.rstrip("\n").split("|")[0] for line in fh.read().splitlines()]
    best = (None, 0)
    i = 0
    while i < len(keys):
        j = i
        while j < len(keys) and keys[j] == keys[i]:
            j += 1
        if j - i > best[1]:
            best = (keys[i], j - i)
        i = j
    return best
